dry_bulk.summary: BDI sits at 3,083 (+1.85σ) with -2.2% ROC60, reflecting a high-end regime historically linked to FFA curve steepening. Capesize rates at 5,105 (+36.1% YTD) reflect resilient Atlantic demand, though Breakwave notes softer Pacific conditions and expanding tonnage lists.
Panamax-Panamax spread at +2,799 points widest since Q4 2023, indicating iron ore/coal voyages crowding out grain demand for smaller vessels.
Handysize rates at 872 (+9.7% YTD) underperform due to weak Atlantic demand and limited fresh enquiry in Mediterranean routes.
China's iron ore imports (1997mt YTD) and steel production (-2.9% YTD) suggest fragile demand, contradicting BDI's momentum despite high levels.
SGX FFA curve shows Capesize backwardation (CWFH26: $22,889/d vs CWFQ26: $35,850/d), signaling near-term weakness despite spot strength.
Dirty tanker Z-score at +1.04σ (2,644) outperforms clean tankers (+0.58σ), reflecting oil market volatility and Suezmax strength.
VLCC TCE at $481,286 (WS475.56) remains elevated, but Breakwave warns of oversupply risks as OPEC+ supply tightness data looms.
dry_bulk.trade_idea: No high-conviction setup: China's August iron ore import data (due 2026-08-25) must show sustained demand to validate BDI's trajectory; otherwise, Capesize longs face mean-reversion risk.
dry_bulk.outlook: Dry bulk momentum hinges on China's August demand data; a rebound in iron ore imports would justify long positioning, while a miss risks sharp correction.
